content.text: Confirmed: `param` comes from a cookie (user-controlled), flows unchanged into `bar`, then directly interpolated into an XPath query string passed to `root.xpath(query)`. The only check is rejecting apostrophes, which doesn't prevent XPath injection via other XPath syntax (e.g., `or`, boolean functions, etc.). This is a genuine XPath injection sink with tainted input.

input.justification: The cookie value 'BenchmarkTest00021' is read via request.cookies.get, URL-decoded, and assigned to 'bar' (since the constant condition 'should' in bar is always true, bar is overwritten with the tainted param). This tainted value is directly concatenated into an XPath expression string (query = f'/Employees/Employee[@emplid=\'{bar}\']') which is then passed to lxml's root.xpath(query). The only mitigation is rejecting single-quote characters, which is insufficient to prevent XPath injection (attackers can still inject boolean conditions, use other XPath operators, or exploit the fact that the quote check can be bypassed with encoding or other injection techniques not using the apostrophe character, e.g. closing the predicate using functions or using 'or' logic without quotes). There is no proper escaping or parameterization of the XPath query, so this is a genuine, exploitable XPath injection vulnerability.
